To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a computational method, based on neural networks, that improves the reliability and sensitivity of peptide identifications made by SEQUEST and provides a reliability estimate for the protein identifications made from these peptide hits.
we have developed a computational method that can be used to improve the sensitivity and specificity in the peptide identification process in tandem mass spectrometer data.

a neural-network-based method for "normalizing SEQUEST scores, combined with a statistical model, improves the reliability of peptide identifications, and hence of protein identifications, compared to the standard procedure in the SEQUEST software package.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational method to improve the reliability of peptide and protein identification in proteomics experiments.
the development and application of novel computational techniques to improve the sensitivity and specificity in peptide identification in mass spectrometer data analysis.
the development of a new computational method for assessing the reliability of peptide identifications made using tandem mass spectrometric data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural network model developed by the authors provides a reliable method for assessing the quality of peptide and protein identifications in tandem mass spectrometer data.

the neural network and statistical model developed here provide a reliable and accurate means for assessing peptide- identification reliability in tandem mass-spectrometry analysis with the SEQUEST algorithm.
the proposed method is a valuable addition to the SEQUEST software package and is a useful tool to help in the interpretation of SEQUENCE results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper describes an algorithm for estimating the reliability for each SEQUEST peptide hit and for each protein identification derived from the peptide hits.
we have developed an automated method for peptide identification in mass spectometry, and also provided an estimate for the reliability of the identifications.
we have developed a reliable and efficient computational method for protein identifications from mass spectrometry data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of protein identification can be estimated from the reliability of peptide identification, and the latter is estimated using our method.
it is possible to develop a method for assessing the reliability of protein identification in tandem mass spectrometer analysis.
the neural network and statistical model approach can be used to provide a rigorous reliability estimate for peptide identification in SEQUEST.
